title: Affine derived pushforward is t-exact and conservative
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. On the derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], the derived direct image $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is t-exact for the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] (restricted to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$) and reflects isomorphisms. Equivalently, an object $E$ of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ lies in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^{\leq n}(X)$ (respectively $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^{\geq n}(X)$) exactly when $Rf_*E$ does, and a morphism is an isomorphism whenever its derived direct image is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ and every integer $i$, the affine cohomology comparison gives $H^i(Rf_*E)\cong f_*H^i(E)$, with the right side quasi-coherent.

The affine comparison transfers cohomology vanishing from E to Rf_*E because ordinary module direct image is additive and therefore preserves zero objects. To reflect vanishing, let M = H^i(E). Place M in degree zero as S = M[0]. The degree-zero cohomology of S is M, and all other cohomology is zero; zero sheaves are quasi-coherent (use the free sheaf on the empty type), so S belongs to D_QCoh(X). If f_*M is zero, the affine cohomology comparison gives zero cohomology for Rf_*S in degree zero and, by the single-object bounds, in every other degree. Use DerivedCategory.isZero_of_forall_isZero_homology to conclude Rf_*S is zero. Consequently the image of the zero endomorphism of S is invertible. Affine conservativity makes the zero endomorphism of S invertible, hence S is zero, and applying H^0 and the single-functor cohomology isomorphism makes M zero. Thus vanishing of each cohomology sheaf is equivalent before and after Rf_*. DerivedCategory.isLE_iff and isGE_iff (def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category) turn these pointwise equivalences into the two bound equivalences.
If $u:E\to F$ has $Rf_*u$ an isomorphism, the affine conservativity statement gives that $u$ is an isomorphism. Thus $Rf_*$ reflects isomorphisms on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$.
